title: Polynomial origin localization reducing to a finite field extension
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is a nonzero local integral domain with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R
e0$. Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-weil-field], with $R\subseteq K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, meaning that every element of $K$ is $r/s$ for $r,s\in R$ and $s
e0$. Suppose $L=K(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ for finitely many elements of $L$. There are $r\ge0$ and a transcendence basis $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ of $L/K$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] such that, putting $K_0=K(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ and $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\subseteq K_0$, the evaluation map $R[X_1,\ldots,X_r]	o P$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is an isomorphism and $P$ is Noetherian. The ideal $\mathfrak n=(\mathfrak m_R,x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ of $P$ is maximal, satisfies $\mathfrak n\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$, and is the kernel of the surjective map $P	o R/\mathfrak m_R$ sending the $x_i$ to zero. The localization $B=P_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], identified with $\{p/s\in K_0:p,s\in P,\ s
otin\mathfrak n\}$, is a Noetherian local integral domain which is not a field, contains $R$, and has $\mathfrak m_B=\mathfrak nB$, $\mathfrak m_B\cap P=\mathfrak n$, and $\mathfrak m_B\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. Both $P$ and $B$ have fraction field $K_0$, and $[L:K_0]<\infty$. If $L/K$ is algebraic, one may take $r=0$, $K_0=K$ and $B=R$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph: choose a transcendence basis and localize the polynomial ring at the origin; expanded construction in the parent's former steps 1--3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] to $L/K$ to choose $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ and put $K_0=K(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. Every $a_i$ is algebraic over $K_0$ by [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. Also $K_0(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=L$: one inclusion holds inside $L$, and the other follows from $K\subseteq K_0$ and $L=K(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], applied over the field $K_0$, gives $[L:K_0]<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph (polynomial origin replacement); explicit verification of the stated replacement.

proof.text: The evaluation map $R[X_1,\ldots,X_r]\to L$ has image $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ by the polynomial construction [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. It is injective: a polynomial that evaluates to zero is zero as a polynomial over $K$, by algebraic independence in [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], and then all its coefficients in the subring $R\subseteq K$ are zero. Thus evaluation identifies $P$ with the polynomial ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to this presentation with zero defining ideal; $P$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph (polynomial origin replacement); explicit verification of the stated replacement.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field], $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ is a field. Define $\epsilon:P\to k$ by taking the constant coefficient modulo $\mathfrak m_R$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. It is onto since constants map onto $k$. Each polynomial is its constant coefficient plus a sum $\sum_i x_i f_i$: assign each nonconstant monomial to one variable dividing it. Therefore $\ker\epsilon=(\mathfrak m_R,x_1,\ldots,x_r)=\mathfrak n$ and $\mathfrak n\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. This kernel is maximal: for an ideal $J$ strictly containing it, choose $f\in J$ with $\epsilon(f)\ne0$ and a constant $c\in R$ mapping to $\epsilon(f)^{-1}$; then $1-cf\in\ker\epsilon\subset J$, so $1\in J$. It is prime because $k$ is a field.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph (polynomial origin replacement); explicit verification of the stated replacement.

proof.text: Inside $K_0$, the set $F=\{p/q:p,q\in P,\ q\ne0\}$ is a field: sums and products use the common-denominator formulas, and a nonzero $p/q$ has inverse $q/p$. It contains $K$, since each element of $K$ is a ratio of elements of $R$, and contains every $x_i$. The definition of $K_0$ as the smallest subfield containing $K$ and the $x_i$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] gives $K_0\subseteq F$; the reverse inclusion holds in $K_0$. Thus $K_0=F$ is the fraction field of $P$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph (polynomial origin replacement); explicit verification of the stated replacement.

proof.text: Localize $P$ at the prime $\mathfrak n$. The fraction description in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies $B$ with $\{p/s\in K_0:s\notin\mathfrak n\}$: denominators are nonzero since $0\in\mathfrak n$, and equality of fractions in either ring is exactly $ps^{\prime}=p^{\prime}s$, since $P$ is a subring of a field. Consequently $R\subseteq P\subseteq B\subseteq K_0$ and $B$ is a nonzero integral domain. The same cited node gives locality and $\mathfrak m_B=\mathfrak nB$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] gives Noetherianity. Finally every $z\in K_0$ is $p/q$ with $p,q\in P\subseteq B$ and $q\ne0$, so $K_0$ is also the fraction field of $B$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph (polynomial origin replacement); explicit verification of the stated replacement.

proof.text: The map $\bar\epsilon:B\to k$, $p/s\mapsto\epsilon(p)/\epsilon(s)$, is well defined by cross multiplication, since $s\notin\ker\epsilon$; the fraction formulas show it is a ring map extending $\epsilon$. It kills $\mathfrak nB$. Hence if $p\in\mathfrak m_B\cap P=\mathfrak nB\cap P$, then $\epsilon(p)=0$, giving $p\in\mathfrak n$; the converse follows from $p=p/1\in\mathfrak nB$. Thus $\mathfrak m_B\cap P=\mathfrak n$ and intersecting with $R$ gives $\mathfrak m_B\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. Choose $0\ne t\in\mathfrak m_R$; it remains nonzero in $B\subseteq K_0$ and belongs to the proper ideal $\mathfrak m_B$. A nonzero element of a proper ideal cannot be a unit, so $B$ is not a field.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph (polynomial origin replacement); explicit verification of the stated replacement.

proof.text: If $L/K$ is algebraic, the empty family is algebraically independent and $L$ is algebraic over $K$, hence is a transcendence basis by [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. Take $r=0$, so $K_0=K$, $P=R$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], every $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak m_R$ has an inverse in $R$. Thus every fraction $p/s$ already belongs to $R$, proving $B=R$ inside $K$. Finiteness follows from the algebraic-generators lemma in step 1, applied with $K_0=K$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, first proof paragraph; Tag 00E9, algebra-lemma-characterize-local-ring, equivalence of (1) and (3) for the zero-variable case.
